language.script_notes: Spanish as national, but bilingual signage is extremely common — Galician in Galicia (close to Portuguese), Basque (Euskara, a language isolate with unmistakable non-Latin-derived words like 'kalea' for street) in the Basque Country/Navarre.

road_furniture.bollard_color: As national — wedge-shaped, orange front reflector, white rear reflectors — with a distinct flat-design, red-square-reflector variant on the AP-15 in Navarre.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: As national; more common on winding coastal and mountain roads.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: As national; Basque-language place-name signage is a strong regional tell where legible.

architecture.roof_style: Steeper pitched roofs than the arid south, built to shed frequent rain.
architecture.roof_material: Slate and dark stone tile more common here than the terracotta that dominates the rest of Spain.
architecture.wall_construction: Stone construction is the defining regional material — grey granite farmhouses and stone field walls, closer in feel to Ireland/Britain/Brittany than to the rest of Spain.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Grey stone tones dominate, a marked contrast to the whitewash and terracotta of the south.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stone hórreos (raised granaries on stilts) dotting the Galician countryside; grey stone farmhouses; modernist Bilbao architecture (Guggenheim) alongside traditional Basque half-timbered houses.

nature.vegetation: Lush green pasture and deciduous/mixed forest, eucalyptus plantations in Galicia — visually closer to Ireland or the UK than to the rest of Spain.
nature.terrain: A green, rugged Atlantic coastline (rías in Galicia, cliffs in Asturias/Cantabria); the Cantabrian Mountains rise close behind the coast.
nature.climate_signature: Oceanic climate — wet, overcast and green much of the year, a strong contrast to the dry sun-bleached feel of the rest of Spain.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 4 around Bilbao/Santiago; thinner and possibly older in remote rural Galicia/Asturias.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coastal and city coverage; sparser in the rural interior mountains.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Green rolling pasture, Atlantic coastline, cool overcast weather, stone field walls
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Green Spain has Spanish/Galician/Basque signage and Spain's national road furniture (wedge bollards, blue-EU-strip plates) rather than UK/Irish left-hand traffic or French Breton signage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same script/plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Green Spain is stone-built and lushly green year-round; the Meseta is flat, dry and golden-brown, and Andalusia is whitewashed and sun-bleached.
